title: Batch APIs — the 50% Discount as Industry Standard

questions.question: What status does BatchDispatcher.openBatch assign before any jobs are processed?
options: completed
failed
queued
in_progress
questions.explanation: openBatch stores a Batch with status queued; addJob is allowed only while that status remains queued.

questions.question: What does BATCH_DISCOUNT=0.50 do to cost_sync?
options: Adds a 50% surcharge
Charges only output tokens
Doubles the cached-input rate
Multiplies the synchronous bill by one half
questions.explanation: cost_batch returns cost_sync(...) * BATCH_DISCOUNT, so the batch price is 50% of the corresponding synchronous bill.

questions.question: How does cost_sync_cache treat the first shared prefix?
options: It pays one CACHE_WRITE_5MIN write, then later calls use CACHED_INPUT
It charges CACHED_INPUT for every document including the first
It removes the prefix from every request
It applies BATCH_DISCOUNT before calculating any input cost
questions.explanation: The function initializes cost with one 5-minute cache write; only iterations with i > 0 add the cheaper cached-input read.

questions.question: What lifecycle does closeBatch implement for a queued batch?
options: It rejects all deferred promises and leaves status queued
It marks in_progress, waits, settles jobs, then marks completed
It marks completed before processing and never waits
It processes only the first job and marks failed
questions.explanation: closeBatch sets status to in_progress, waits for turnaroundMs, resolves or rejects every job, awaits settlements, and then sets completed.

questions.question: What label does fakeClassifier return when input.text.length is even?
options: neutral
negative
positive
failed
questions.explanation: The parity expression selects positive for even lengths and neutral for odd lengths; the marked option is the local positive branch.

questions.question: Why can BATCH + CACHE approach roughly 10% of the synchronous bill in the lesson's headline example?
options: Batching removes all output-token charges
The cache write is free after the first request
The batch API changes the model's output length
It stacks a 50% batch multiplier on a large saving from cached repeated prefixes
questions.explanation: cost_batch_cache halves cost_sync_cache, and the repeated prefix makes most later input reads much cheaper; the exact ratio depends on the workload mix.
